plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree prized in East Asia that produces fragrant five-petaled blossoms on bare branches, often while frost or snow is still present. It is a cherished harbinger of spring in gardens, temples, and orchards.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (February to March)
plants.location: China, Japan, Korea; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms bloom earlier than cherry blossoms and symbolize perseverance and hope in East Asian culture because they flower in the cold.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers surrounded by paler outer petals, found in woodlands and meadows. Its blue-green strap-like leaves emerge in late winter, and flowers carpet the ground in early spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (March to April)
plants.location: Western Europe, including the UK, France, and Spain; widely naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: Daffodils contain the compound galantamine, which is used in medication for Alzheimer's disease, and the flower is the national emblem of Wales, celebrated on March 1.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: An Australian evergreen shrub or small tree covered in fluffy, fragrant golden ball-shaped flower clusters. It grows in woodlands and open forests and is a major nectar and pollen source for native insects and birds.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in Australia, with some flowering from July to October; scattered bloom can occur in other seasons depending on region and conditions
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia, and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1.

plants.name: Crocus vernus
plants.description: A small cormous perennial that pushes up goblet-shaped flowers through lingering snow in alpine meadows and lawns. The blooms open in sunshine and close in cloudy weather or at night.
plants.location: Mountain meadows of the Alps and Pyrenees in Europe; widely cultivated in temperate gardens
plants.funFact: Spring crocuses are an important early food source for emerging bees, though they are not the source of saffron, which comes from the autumn-flowering Crocus sativus.
